rules.description: Use provider-managed network and application DDoS mitigation without treating ordinary traffic spikes as attacks.
exceptions: capacity and sensitivity overrides remain provider-plan/operator settings
rules.rationale: Managed adaptive mitigation absorbs volumetric attacks without a guessed static default-deny rule.

rules.description: Preserve access for provider-verified search crawlers while retaining managed exploit inspection.
rules.rationale: Avoid SEO false positives without trusting spoofable user-agent strings.

rules.description: Exclude explicitly reviewed monitoring and internal-automation CIDRs from generic bot challenges while retaining managed exploit inspection.
exceptions: lists must be explicit, minimal, owned, and reviewed
rules.rationale: Known service traffic should remain reliable without becoming a broad WAF bypass.

rules.description: Allow ordinary browser traffic that has no corroborated automation or abuse signal.
exceptions: managed WAF and route limits still evaluate independently
rules.rationale: The baseline must not force challenges on normal users.

rules.description: Use provider managed rules for injection, XSS, file inclusion, command injection, exploit signatures and protocol anomalies.
exceptions: verified signed webhook traffic may require route-specific managed-rule exceptions
rules.rationale: Stage managed protections before broad enforcement.

rules.description: Detect methods other than GET, HEAD and OPTIONS on the static public hostname.
exceptions: future dynamic routes must be moved to an API hostname before enabling write methods
rules.rationale: GitHub Pages does not require write methods for static delivery.

rules.description: Challenge path traversal and common scanner/probing request patterns.
rules.rationale: High-signal probing should not reach the origin unchecked.

rules.description: Observe excessive URI, query, header, and plan-supported body sizes before any blocking promotion.
exceptions: trusted operational CIDRs remain visible to managed WAF
rules.rationale: Oversized metadata is suspicious but can have legitimate edge cases, so the baseline observes first.

rules.description: Challenge suspicious unverified automation without blocking all non-browser clients.
rules.rationale: Use behavioral/provider signals and challenge uncertain automation.

rules.description: Provide a disabled, time-bounded block template for sources that repeatedly fail managed challenges and have corroborating abuse evidence.
rules.rationale: A permanent block is unsafe; incident responders may instantiate only a reviewed expiring quarantine rule.

rules.description: Observe or challenge anonymous proxy, VPN and Tor signals according to route sensitivity.
exceptions: never create a permanent deny from an unverified reputation signal alone
rules.rationale: Reputation is corroborating evidence, not identity.

rules.description: Observe high-volume static asset requests with a generous baseline threshold.
rules.rationale: Detect abusive asset scraping without interfering with normal page loads.

rules.description: Observe excessive HTML document request rates per source IP.
rules.rationale: Baseline crawl protection for static documents.

rules.description: Limit authentication attempts on dynamic origins using identity/session counters where available.
rules.rationale: Reduce credential-stuffing velocity while preserving legitimate retries.

rules.description: Constrain password-reset initiation on dynamic origins.
rules.rationale: Reduce reset abuse and enumeration pressure.

rules.description: Observe expensive or high-volume search requests on dynamic origins.
rules.rationale: Protect future server-side search resources without guessing current load.

rules.description: Constrain contact/form submissions on dynamic endpoints while preserving the external Formspree integration.
exceptions: external Formspree destination is not an application origin route
rules.rationale: Reduce automated form abuse without breaking the static frontend integration.

rules.description: Apply a broad observe-only API baseline before route-specific production tuning.
exceptions: signed webhooks require independent source/signature-aware policy
rules.rationale: Safe initial API visibility without asserting current backend capacity.

rules.description: Constrain administrative routes and combine with explicit operator-approved geo/ASN controls if needed.
exceptions: trusted corporate CIDRs when explicitly configured
rules.rationale: Administrative surfaces require stricter abuse resistance.

rules.description: Observe webhook volume and prefer cryptographic sender verification over browser challenges.
exceptions: verified signed webhook senders must not receive interactive challenges
rules.rationale: Webhook authentication is cryptographic; rate limiting is supplemental.

rules.description: Keep country and ASN enforcement disabled until an operator explicitly approves a scoped policy.
rules.rationale: Geo/ASN restrictions are high false-positive controls and are opt-in.

rules.description: Enforce transport/browser security headers at the edge and start CSP in report-only mode.
rules.rationale: GitHub Pages cannot reliably set these application-owned headers.

rules.description: Cache reviewed static assets at the edge with conservative TTLs and a host/path/query-safe cache key.
exceptions: responses with Set-Cookie, private, no-store, authorization, or personalized semantics
rules.rationale: Edge caching reduces origin pressure while retaining rapid static-site rollback.

rules.description: Bypass edge caching for authentication, account, checkout, admin, webhook, and personalized API responses.
exceptions: an API route may be cached only under an explicit public-data contract and reviewed cache key
rules.rationale: Sensitive responses must never become shared cache entries.

rules.description: Track the accepted limitation that GitHub Pages cannot require authenticated edge-to-origin access.
rules.rationale: Do not claim non-bypassable origin protection until the static origin is migrated.

rules.description: Require private ingress, authenticated origin pulls, mTLS, provider egress allow lists, or an edge-overwritten secret header for future dynamic origins.
exceptions: GitHub Pages is not eligible for this control
rules.rationale: Dynamic services need a non-bypassable edge-to-origin trust boundary before public routing.

rules.description: Export security metadata without cookies, authorization headers, passwords or complete sensitive query values.
rules.rationale: Collect enough evidence for response without unnecessary sensitive-data retention.

rules.description: Provide a disabled emergency managed-challenge template that requires owner, incident reference, and expiry within 24 hours.
rules.rationale: Emergency controls must be reversible, targeted, and time bounded rather than permanent lockdown.
